summary: Phase A INFRA half, docs and stubs only, nothing installed on the VPS. SPE-4789/4793: GREPTIME_* placement under /etc/substrate/substrate.env with the tailnet-forwarder-preferred / public-HTTPS-Basic-fallback order, plus OTEL / MCP-audit / evidence env names reserved as placeholders; gateway.env.example marks its GREPTIME_* copy TRANSITIONAL because substrate-mcp owns the store credential. SPE-4792: systemd oneshot+timer and cron sketch for the seat lease heartbeat with env names only, the TIMEOUT < INTERVAL <= TTL/3 invariant, and a read-only credential-free drift-probe.sh feeding coord.drift_scan(repo). No secrets, no values, no probe transcripts restated from prior receipts. No AddMcpServer for Greptime. services/** untouched. Second tip: five Greptile P1s (4141814747, 4141814758, 4141814773, 4141814784, 4141814794) all verified as real and fixed — the JSON receipt was being swallowed by .gitignore, ls-remote had no timeout, an empty or malformed reachability target list exited 0, and the unit's TimeoutStartSec plus the timer's RandomizedDelaySec were fixed literals that broke the cadence guarantee. Third tip: Greptile P1 4141898005 (an unattempted git lookup reporting success) verified and fixed at the root — both *_TIMEOUT_S values are now validated before any probe runs, and 'never ran' is separated from 'ran and failed' in both sub-probes. The same defect was found and fixed in the reachability probe, which Greptile had not flagged. Head branch renamed to bot-05-infrastructure/* so G-1 can attribute the change. Fourth tip (LEAD GO, PR #38 after #36 was closed by the head-branch rename): INFRA unit sketch for the lease sweeper — substrate-lease-reap.{service,timer} calling the SYSTEMS-owned coord_reap_leases on the loopback substrate-mcp, default 45s within a 30-60s band, with the bearer kept in a root-only curl config file so no credential reaches the unit or a process listing. On-demand reaping through the MCP tool is retained and stays SYSTEMS'; the timer is only a sweeper for quiet load.

claims.claim: The ownership manifest still validates after adding infra/substrate/ and infra/lease-heartbeat/.

Every path this change touches, including both receipt files, resolves to bot-05-infrastructure (G-1 PASS). ownership.yaml itself was not edited: its bare README.md rule sends a README at any depth to QUALITY, so the two prose files are named SUBSTRATE-ENV.md and LEASE-HEARTBEAT.md instead.
G-3 finds no secret in any touched file, including the two env examples and this receipt.
G-7 desk integrity is unaffected: no roster, pack, prompt or template was touched, so no Greptime MCP server was registered and no tool was added.
drift-probe.sh is syntactically valid bash.
The git-tip probe reports local tip, branch, dirty flag, remote tip and the ahead/behind relation without fetching, and correctly resolved 'ahead' against origin/main.
The reachability probe distinguishes an open port, a closed port and a malformed target in one run, and a closed port does not abort the remaining probes.
drift-probe.sh all emits parseable JSON with both sub-probes, and exits 0 while reporting an unreachable target — probe status is separate from probe result.
All four GREPTIME_* names (URL, USER, PASSWORD, DB) are present in the substrate env example.
The only non-empty values in the substrate env example are a loopback host, a port, a log level and the database name 'public' — no credential and no public domain.
The heartbeat unit is Type=oneshot driven by the timer's OnUnitActiveSec, reads its env from /etc/desk-lease-heartbeat/heartbeat.env, and its ExecStart names the not-yet-existing SYSTEMS entrypoint.
No install.sh exists in infra/lease-heartbeat/, so nothing installs the stub unit that would fail every tick.

Greptile P1 4141814747 confirmed, not refuted: .gitignore line 5 (.receipts/**/*.json) silently excluded the JSON receipt from the first commit, so the PR carried only the Markdown half and G-2 would have found no receipt for this task.
The JSON receipt is now tracked in git, force-added past that ignore rule the way the seat's existing .json receipts are. .gitignore itself is unowned in ownership.yaml, so it was not edited.
Greptile P1 4141814758 reproduced: a bare git ls-remote against an unresponsive remote does not return on its own and had to be killed by an outer cap.
With DRIFT_GIT_TIMEOUT_S the same lookup returns bounded, reports the timeout in 'note', and keeps exit 0 because a timed-out remote is a probe result rather than a probe that could not be attempted.
Greptile P1 4141814773 fixed for the empty case: an empty target list now exits 3 with ok:false instead of exiting 0 with an empty target array.
Greptile P1 4141814773 fixed for the malformed case: a malformed target is counted and exits 3, while the well-formed target beside it is still probed and reported.
A fully well-formed run still exits 0 and reports an open port up and a closed port down, so tightening the configuration checks did not turn an ordinary outage into a script failure.
Greptile P1 4141814794 and 4141814784 addressed in the units: TimeoutStartSec and RandomizedDelaySec are both marked PLACEHOLDER and generated at install time alongside OnUnitActiveSec.
Greptile P1 4141898005 confirmed, and worse than reported: on the pushed tip an invalid DRIFT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S also produced UNPARSEABLE JSON (timeout_s:abc emitted unquoted) while still exiting 0.
Root cause fixed at the source: both *_TIMEOUT_S values are validated before any probe runs, and a bad one stops the run with a config object and exit 3 instead of a misleading result.
A git lookup that could not be STARTED now reports ok:false with remote_checked:false and exits 3, so a caller trusting 'ok' can no longer read an unchecked remote tip as a completed check.
The same defect in the reachability probe is fixed: a connect that could not be started reports probed:false and is counted in targets_unattempted rather than claiming the target is down.
The ordinary paths still behave after the tightening: a good run exits 0 with remote_checked true, an open port up and a closed port down.
A timed-out remote is still treated as a probe result rather than a failure: ok stays true, remote_checked is false, and the exit stays 0.
Duration validation rejects a non-numeric value, a unit suffix, zero and a negative, and accepts an integer and a decimal, keeping timeout_s numeric in the JSON.
The head branch was renamed to bot-05-infrastructure/substrate-env-lease-stubs-1s6sf0, so the gates job's acting-bot step can now attribute this change; the receipt's branch field matches.
The two new sweeper units and the docs they change stay inside bot-05-infrastructure ownership.
G-3 finds no secret in the sweeper units or the updated env example.
Both sweeper units verify clean under systemd-analyze, so the ExecStart line continuations and Timer stanza parse as systemd intends.

Neither sweeper unit contains a credential, a token name or a Bearer literal: the bearer is reached through a root-only curl config file named by SUBSTRATE_LEASE_REAP_CURL_CONFIG, so it never reaches a command line visible in ps or systemctl show.
All five sweeper env names are present: SUBSTRATE_MCP_URL, SUBSTRATE_LEASE_REAP_INTERVAL_SEC, SUBSTRATE_LEASE_REAP_TIMEOUT_SEC, SUBSTRATE_LEASE_REAP_CURL_CONFIG, SUBSTRATE_LEASE_REAP_REQUEST.
The heartbeat env example remains names-only after the addition — every value is still empty.
The sweeper timer carries the documented 45s default, within the sanctioned 30-60s band, and is deliberately not Persistent.
The coord_reap_leases request body documented in LEASE-HEARTBEAT.md parses as JSON and names the tool with no arguments.

G-2 run against this receipt reports exactly one problem, the null approved_by: no bypass command, no claim citing a failing or non-existent command, and no vague unverified entry. Approval is QUALITY's to add.

unverified: Nothing was installed or restarted on the VPS: the heartbeat unit/timer are stubs whose ExecStart target under services/desk-lease-heartbeat does not exist yet (SYSTEMS), and no install.sh was written on purpose

No live Greptime, Timescale, Dragonfly, Hindsight or RAGFlow probe was run from this session; the SPE-4789 receipts infra-spe4789-greptime-place-env and infra-spe4789-agent-events-append-mode remain the only evidence for the placement and the tailnet startup timeout, and neither is restated here
The reachability probe was exercised only against loopback (a local python http.server on 8123, a closed port, and a malformed target) — never against a tailscale-forwarder host, which needs the VPS
GREPTIME_URL on the VPS is still the public HTTPS + Basic fallback; the tailnet cutover and the G-6 retirement of public exposure are not part of this change
The suggested drift_scan snapshot shape in DRIFT-SCAN.md §4 is a proposal to SYSTEMS, not an accepted interface; contracts/tool-rosters is QUALITY-owned and was not touched
LEASE_TTL_S and LEASE_INTERVAL_S values, and the renew subcommand's exit-code contract, are open on SYSTEMS (DRIFT-SCAN.md §5, LEASE-HEARTBEAT.md §5)
approved_by stays null until QUALITY reviews; G-2 fails closed on that field by design

The cadence invariant now includes the jitter term (INTERVAL + JITTER <= TTL/3) and all three unit literals are generated at install time — but no installer exists yet to enforce it, so the guarantee is documented, not executed
Quality Gates has not yet been observed passing on the renamed bot-05-infrastructure/* branch — the rename satisfies the acting-bot regex locally, but only a CI run proves the remaining gates green

The sweeper is not installed and has never been run against a live substrate-mcp: coord_reap_leases has not been called, so neither the tool name, its argument shape, nor its response on a sweep with nothing to reap is confirmed (LEASE-HEARTBEAT.md §5 asks SYSTEMS for all three)
systemd-analyze verify parses the sweeper units but does not execute them; the ${...} expansions in ExecStart are unresolved because no EnvironmentFile exists on this host
rollback_plan: Docs and stub unit files only; nothing is installed, enabled or restarted, and no live env file was edited. Revert the two commits on the branch, or close the draft PR — there is no host state to undo and no data implication. The one behavioural note is documentary: gateway.env.example now marks its GREPTIME_* block TRANSITIONAL, which changes no running gateway because install.sh never overwrites a live /etc/desk-gateway/gateway.env.
